clue.text: Copper and cleric's fight for prime arena location

parts.note: a copper is a police officer; DI is a detective inspector
a rector is a parish priest, here in the possessive
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A policeman and a vicar come to blows over the best seats in the stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium's private enclosure for club officials is the most privileged viewing spot in the ground.

clue.text: Came by doctor and Pope upset with row

indicators.note: upset signals that the letters of the word Pope are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: A physician arrived and the pontiff was troubled by a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles POPE into OPPE; 'row' is the noisy kind, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To come by is an idiom for paying a casual, unannounced visit.

clue.text: Regularly ignored droopy tail of Rex?

indicators.note: every other letter of the words droopy tail is skipped, starting with the first, and the rest are kept

explanation.surface: A dog called Rex has a sagging tail that keeps being overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex looks like a dog's name, but it is Latin for king, so the definition asks for something belonging to a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Rex is the Latin word for king, so anything of the king is regal or kingly.

clue.text: Feat cutting 101 plants

indicators.note: cutting means the deed word goes into the middle of the number, splitting it

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals
a feat is a deed or act

explanation.surface: An achievement of trimming a hundred and one plants.
explanation.definitionFit: These spiny desert succulents are a family of plants.

clue.text: Teacher dismissing of supporting work one dictates

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other, so the teacher remnant goes under work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: dismissing tells us to send away the letters of the word of from the teacher

parts.note: a professor is a university teacher
taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic gives up backing some piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' only makes sense in a down answer, where the piece doing the supporting is written below the other one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant who dictates to others and rules harshly fits the definition; dictates here is a verb with one as its subject.

clue.text: Second mate's at sea in boat

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of mate's are jumbled

parts.note: in means fashionable, as does hip

explanation.surface: A ship's second mate is out on the water in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges MATES into TEAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel driven by steam engines is a kind of boat, loosely used for any ship.

clue.text: Attack is concerning group

parts.note: on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds
a set is a group or collection

explanation.surface: An assault concerns a particular group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun can mean an assault or onslaught, as in the start of an enemy offensive.

clue.text: Spa gets in poolside bouncers

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
to board a vehicle is to get in it

explanation.surface: A health spa lets in people beside the pool to do some bouncing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncers' suggests door staff, but the things doing the bouncing are the flexible diving planks.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers bounce on these flexible planks at the edge of a swimming pool before leaping in.

clue.text: Representative for unknown figures

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
in algebra x and y are the usual unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A delegate stands in for figures nobody knows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in authorised to act or vote on another's behalf is a representative.

clue.text: Strains on exterior of cherry trees

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after, so the strains follow the outer letters of cherry
exterior of picks the outside letters of the word cherry, its first and last

parts.note: to strain is to press hard, so strains means presses

explanation.surface: Something weighs on the skin of a cherry growing on trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Coniferous evergreens often planted in graveyards and Mediterranean gardens are trees.

clue.text: We might reckon on these picnic blankets

parts.note: a spread is a feast laid out, as at a picnic
sheets, like blankets, are bed coverings

explanation.surface: Picnic blankets sound like something we could count on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rugs on the grass; 'reckon' means calculate, pointing to accounting software grids.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer programs laid out in grids of cells are used for calculating, or reckoning, figures.

clue.text: Is plum off? I have rash

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters of is plum are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone worries that their plum has gone bad and that they have a skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like the skin complaint; it is the adjective for hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on sudden urges without thought is what being reckless or hasty means.

clue.text: Measure space rock that's out of the ordinary

indicators.note: out of means the letter for ordinary has been taken away from the space rock

parts.note: a meteor is a rock from space
O is short for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: Gauging a remarkable rock from outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the ordinary' reads as unusual but splits into a deletion of O. O level was the British school exam at the Ordinary level.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that gauges quantities such as gas or electricity used is a measuring instrument; also the American spelling of the length unit.

clue.text: 'They're divine' — some obsessed dog-lovers reflected

indicators.note: reflected means the selected run of letters is read backwards, as in a mirror
some means only part of the words obsessed dog-lovers is used

explanation.surface: Fanatical dog fans think their pets are heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' looks like 'thought about'; it turns the letters back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Female deities are divine beings, so the plural fits a statement about what is divine.

clue.text: Doctor Anne cured patient suffering

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of Anne cured are altered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician called Anne healed someone who was ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' and 'patient' set a medical scene; 'patient' is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing hardship patiently over a long time is stamina or fortitude.

clue.text: Crooked, extremely slick partners above suspicion

indicators.note: in a down answer the bridge partners sit on top of the suspicion
extremely takes the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word slick

parts.note: East and West are partners at the bridge table
a whiff is a hint or suspicion of something

explanation.surface: Smooth associates who are beyond reproach are actually crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The British slang term means askew or lopsided, not dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked here means askew, lopsided or not straight, which the British slang word describes.

clue.text: African native bringing foreign money into centre of Chad

indicators.note: bringing, paired with into, says the currency is carried inside the other letters
into marks where the foreign money goes: within the middle letters of Chad
centre of picks the middle letters of the word Chad

parts.note: the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: A local brings foreign cash into the middle of Chad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African native' looks like a person; it is an animal native to Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: This scavenging carnivore with a laughing call is a creature native to Africa.

clue.text: Testers set up cutting tool with pit workers

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word is turned upward, reading bottom to top

parts.note: an axe is a cutting tool
miners work down a coal pit

explanation.surface: Assessors arrange a chopping tool alongside coal workers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who set and mark exams test candidates' knowledge.

clue.text: Confessed wearing dress to need front scrubbed

indicators.note: front scrubbed means the leading letter is wiped away

parts.note: gowned means dressed in a gown

explanation.surface: Someone admitted to putting on a frock and needing to clean the front of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confessed' is the sense of owned up.
explanation.definitionFit: To own, as in own up, is to admit or acknowledge something.

clue.text: Maybe the French Open and US are to be rearranged

indicators.note: plainly says the letters of open, US and are are to be put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The French Open and US Open tennis tournaments are being rescheduled.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like tennis scheduling; 'Maybe' marks the French as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The French are one example of the peoples of a European continent, hence Maybe.

clue.text: Part of helicopter shelled from hill

indicators.note: shelled means the outer letters of the word from are removed, leaving its inside

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A helicopter component was stripped off a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: Tor is a word used in south-west England for a rocky hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning blade assembly overhead is the component that lifts a helicopter.

clue.text: Wind engulfs island city abroad

indicators.note: engulfs means the twisting word swallows up the island letter

parts.note: to wind, rhyming with find, is to twist or turn

explanation.surface: A gale swallows an island city overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like a gale but is the verb for twisting.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern Italian city is a foreign place from a British setter's view.

clue.text: We with a self-confidence gaining new convert for hostile use

indicators.note: gaining means the self-assurance takes in the letter for new

parts.note: poise is calm self-assurance

explanation.surface: We, with assurance, take on a new convert to use against the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something into a weapon is to adapt it for attacking an enemy.

clue.text: High Street store contracted Northern Gas

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the store name loses its last letter

parts.note: Argos is a British catalogue retail chain found on many high streets

explanation.surface: A chain shop cut back on its northern gas supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Argos is a well-known British catalogue shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An inert noble element, used in light bulbs, is a gas.

clue.text: Venture from old wood

parts.note: pine is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Taking a risk with antique timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venture' looks like an enterprise; it is the verb, as in venture an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture a view is to state it tentatively, to give an opinion.

clue.text: Withdrawing from holy place after sacrificing the last monarch

indicators.note: after means the monarch comes after the shortened holy place
sacrificing the last means the holy place gives up its final letter

parts.note: a shrine is a holy place
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A king pulls out of a temple after making an offering.
explanation.definitionFit: Recoiling or drawing back in fear or distaste is withdrawing.

clue.text: It holds writer back being useless

indicators.note: holds means the word it contains the reversed writing tool
back means the writing tool is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: Something prevents an author from being any use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun in the surface, but its two letters are taken as they are and wrap round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy and incompetent people are useless at what they attempt.

clue.text: Home designer revamped housing by following pointers

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: housing means the remade letters enclose the other pieces
revamped means remade, so the letters of designer are reworked

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in two by four
F is the abbreviation for following, as in pp. 6f

explanation.surface: An interior designer renovated a house by following tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revamped' rearranges DESIGNER into DEINGERS, which holds XF after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The digit next to the thumb is the one people use to point, so these are pointers.
